title: Ansel and the Sigil
premise: Rafael Ishikawa has hidden her beast-speaker gift since magic was outlawed, selling harmless charms in the walled city of Corvane while the old gods fall silent. When prayers begin to be answered again—twisted, hungry, and wrong—Rafael is drawn into the ruins beneath the city with Ansel, a disgraced covenant-keeper who once broke the pact between realms to save her own life. Together they must gather the scattered sigils of the old covenant and confront the truth that the gods' silence was Rafael's family's doing, a bargain her mother struck that is now expiring. To reforge the covenant before the last dragon-fire gutters out, Rafael must sacrifice her memories of Ansel, ending the book with a covenant restored, magic lawful, and Ansel choosing to love her all over again from the beginning.
about_author: Wren Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms and oral histories in coastal mill towns. Ansel and the Sigil is their second novel, following the quietly acclaimed The Saltwright's Daughter.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She sells a luck-knot to a grieving fisherman and privately murmurs a word to his dying gull, which answers—a crime. Establishes her hidden gift, her poverty, and the city's fear. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: The God That Answered
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A shrine prayer is answered overnight: a blind child sees, but his eyes now reflect a second moon. Rafael recognizes the wrongness of old power returning unbound. Beat: dread replacing wonder.

chapters.title: Ansel at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The disgraced covenant-keeper arrives in Corvane hunting the source of the answered prayers and recognizes Rafael's gift in the market. Beat: wary recognition—two people who each thought they were the last of something.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Ansel confronts her; she denies everything, then breaks when her rat-friend Sable speaks her name aloud. Ansel reveals the covenant between realms was broken, not faded. Beat: the relief and terror of being known.

chapters.title: What Her Mother Buried
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, flashback-woven. She searches her late mother's charm-shop cellar and finds a sigil-stone and a confession: her mother's bargain caused the gods' silence. Beat: inheritance as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: The Undercity of Roots
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ansel leads Rafael into the ruins beneath Corvane where the covenant was once sworn; living roots still hum with dead oaths. Beat: awe shadowed by grief for what was lost.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Her beast allies warn that the answered prayers are a predator wearing godhood. Sable offers to guide them but demands a memory as payment. Beat: the theme of memory as currency made literal.

chapters.title: The First Sigil: Ash
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They claim the sigil of ash from a burned temple, but Ansel freezes—she was the one who shattered the covenant here years ago. Beat: guilt confessed, trust tested.

chapters.title: The Warden of Prayers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The city's magic-hunting Warden catches Sable and begins tracing the answered prayers back to Rafael. Beat: hunted; duty of the state versus duty of conscience.

chapters.title: Fire That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They find the last dragon, Emberling, guttering in a mountain caldera—dragon-fire is the covenant's fuel, and it is nearly spent. Beat: urgency crystallizes; the deadline is made flesh.

chapters.title: The Price of the Second Sigil
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The sigil of tide demands a true memory in exchange; Rafael gives up her mother's face. Beat: love against duty—she pays to save a world that outlawed her.

chapters.title: Ansel's Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, full flashback. Twelve years ago Ansel shattered the covenant to stop a god from consuming her city, believing she'd saved it; instead she silenced the gods and doomed the dragons. Beat: villain and hero collapse into one grieving person.

chapters.title: The Warden's Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The Warden offers Rafael freedom in exchange for betraying Ansel; Rafael sees her own fear of exposure weaponized. Beat: temptation of the safe, small life.

chapters.title: The Third Sigil: Bone
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In the catacombs they take the sigil of bone from the covenant's first dead keeper, who briefly wakes and judges Ansel worthy of a second chance. Beat: absolution neither of them believes they deserve.

chapters.title: Sable's Memory, Returned
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Sable returns Rafael's payment unspent, revealing the predator-god fears beasts because beasts remember what gods were before worship. Beat: loyalty rewarded; hope kindled.

chapters.title: The God of Answered Prayers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The predator-god, Hollow-Voice, offers Rafael everything she's wanted: legitimacy, safety, love without sacrifice. Beat: the antagonist's true power—making surrender feel like homecoming.

chapters.title: Refusal in the Market Square
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael publicly speaks with beasts before the whole city, exposing herself to save a child from Hollow-Voice's answer. Beat: the climactic choice of self over invisibility.

chapters.title: Guttering
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Emberling's fire nearly dies; the fourth sigil, ember, can only be lit by a willing sacrifice of memory. Rafael volunteers without telling Ansel what it will cost. Beat: love against duty at its sharpest.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the caldera, Rafael and Ansel swear the new covenant with all four sigils as Hollow-Voice attacks; Emberling blazes one final time. Beat: climax—sacrifice, chaos, and the covenant catching flame.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair Across the Fire
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The covenant holds, magic is lawful, but Rafael remembers nothing of Ansel—her memories were the price. Ansel keeps his distance, honoring what she gave. Beat: bittersweet victory; grief without a name.

chapters.title: A Stranger Who Stays
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel stays in Corvane, selling charms beside Rafael, telling her their story one piece at a time without asking anything back. Beat: patience as devotion; memory rebuilt through retelling.

chapters.title: The Sigil in Her Palm
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael finds the ash sigil warm in her hand and a feeling she can't source—like a word remembered by the body. She asks Ansel to start again from the beginning. Beat: resolution—love outlasting memory; the covenant, like them, reforged.
